A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same RNA study. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched across the reorganization.

before.justification: v3 reports original Zephyr-7B experiments on WMDP and MMLU, including perturbation tests, noise-scale analyses and layer ablations.

after.justification: v4 retains these experiments and adds assumption diagnostics, adversarial evaluations, capability benchmarks and Llama/Mistral results.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the same Gaussian perturbation of reference-model retain representations during fine-tuning, with perturbed representations or logits supplying RM/PO retain targets. The added explanations and evaluations do not change RNA's procedure or objectives.

E1.justification: v4 adds TruthfulQA, ToxiGen, WinoGrande, CommonsenseQA, HellaSwag, ARC Easy/Challenge and BoolQ evaluation, plus adversarially perturbed MMLU scenarios (Appendices F–G). This substantially broadens the retained WMDP, WikiText and MMLU coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the base model, RMU, Adaptive RMU, RSV, and NPO/DPO/SimNPO with KL or MSE retain losses. Tables 6–7 reuse this set; Table 8 applies RMU and NPO+KL to added backbones. The attack algorithms introduce stress-test protocols, not competing unlearning methods.

E3.justification: New settings include Llama-3-8B/Mistral-7B configurations, GCG/TextBugger/DeepWordBug/TextFooler attacks evaluated with AuA and ROUGE-L, and ten-token greedy generation for layer-7 MaxAct diagnostics. Appendix A.4 also changes the reported SimNPO+MSE retain weights (biology, cyber) from (5, 10) to (10, 5); this does not establish that existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix C adds loss-change distributions examining the convexity-based argument and activation-change diagnostics supporting Assumption 4.1. Appendix F newly tests whether RNA increases susceptibility to other attacks. Existing n-gram, noise-scale and layer analyses are retained; moving the bi-gram analysis to Appendix D is not an addition.

E5.justification: No new run/seed counts, confidence intervals or significance tests are reported. Existing noise-sensitivity boxplots are retained; the added histograms describe diagnostic distributions rather than uncertainty in comparative performance.

E6.justification: Figures 8–9 and Tables 6–8 add diagnostic, attack, capability and cross-model findings. For example, new Llama-3-8B NPO+KL results report perturbed-MMLU accuracy of 26.2 without RNA versus 47.3 with RNA, alongside poorer forgetting: WMDP accuracy rises from 27.9 to 33.2. These are added settings, not version-to-version gains. Table 3 also corrects RMU+RNA WMDP accuracy from 28.8 to 28.7.

T1.justification: The main assumptions, theorems and Appendix B proof conclusions remain unchanged; the Euclidean-norm notation changes are equivalent. Appendix C.1 adds the case of a local maximum with a negative definite Hessian, explaining why Equation 9's inequality would reverse—a limited mathematical qualification.

C1.justification: v4 replaces the abstract's absolute claim of no additional computational overhead with a lightweight description, while retaining the no-extra-forward-pass explanation. The central contributions remain unchanged. The abstract's stronger emphasis on hiding rather than erasing knowledge repeats an interpretation already present in v3 Section 5.1.

C2.justification: v4 adds explanations involving gradient sensitivity, loss-landscape smoothing and blurred trigger boundaries, and discusses the applicability of its convexity and Gaussian assumptions. New discussions address method-dependent attack effects and cross-model forgetting trade-offs. Appendix I additionally explains the benchmark restriction and updates the model-size limitation to 7B/8B.

D1.justification: Appendix H supplies model-specific coefficients, retain weights and RNA noise scales; Appendix C.2 specifies generation length, decoding and activation-measurement details. Appendix A.4 removes the supplementary-implementation statement, while the code URL, hardware disclosure and promised perturbed-dataset release remain.

R1.justification: v4 adds robustness-trade-off literature, references supporting the new evaluations, and newer unlearning work including Wang et al. (2025a), Wu et al. (2025) and Zhuang et al. (2025). Several random-noise-defense citations are removed from the RNA motivation. The central retain-versus-forget robustness positioning remains.

P1.justification: v4 rewrites the abstract, locally reorganizes Sections 2 and 5, expands explanations and moves the bi-gram discussion into Appendix D. Author information and citation style change, and an AI-usage declaration is added. Much of the existing method, theory and results prose remains closely matched.

P2.justification: Figure 1 moves from a large 2-by-2 introductory display to four much smaller horizontal results panels, with revised axis ranges and labels. v4 adds Figures 8–9 and Tables 6–8, relocates existing plots, changes table styling and substantially reformats the document.

improvement.justification: The new cross-model, attack and capability tests make RNA's generalization and side effects more assessable, including forgetting trade-offs absent from v3's evaluation. Assumption diagnostics and limitations also improve scrutiny. The net gain is limited: the diagnostics remain indirect, attack specifications are incomplete, and Figure 1 is less legible. Some new interpretations overstate results: Appendix F claims uniform degradation, although Table 6 reports GCG accuracy of 40.7 for NPO+MSE versus 40.3 for the base model.
